text:
maria: CI wheels all green, but nightly perf shows a 18% regression on our L1 latency benchmark. investigation below.

ci-bot: build 2026-02-18T09:12:34Z - manylinux wheel uploaded: redwood_attn-0.9.1-cp38-manylinux2014_x86_64.whl :white_check_mark:

maria: running the same binary in staging shows kernel selection falling back to fused_attn_plain instead of flash_attn_paged. runtime log: `selected_kernel=fused_attn_plain reason=kernel_init_failure(symbol_version_mismatch)`

devon: that sounds like a symbol mismatch at load time. can you paste `ldd` + `nm` of the wheel shared object?

maria: sure, snippet: 
```
$ ldd /opt/redwood/lib/python3.8/site-packages/redwood_attn/_kernels.cpython-38-x86_64-linux-gnu.so
libc.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 (0x7f8c...)\n
$ nm -D _kernels.cpython-38-x86_64-linux-gnu.so | grep flash_attn_init
0000000000102f40 T flash_attn_init
0000000000103040 T paged_flash_init
0000000000103200 T fused_attn_plain_init
```

maria: but runtime message shows unresolved symbol `__atomic_fetch_add_8` when loading flash kernel on bookworm worker.

ashok: that atomic symbol is provided by libatomic when built with older gcc toolchains. manylinux2014 wheels target glibc but sometimes depend on libatomic if compiled with -latomic implicitly. which compiler was used for the wheel build?

ci-bot: builder image: quay.io/redwood/ci-wheels:debian-bookworm-gcc-12-2025-01-10

devon: gcc12 on bookworm can produce libatomic deps. our staging runtime base image is debian-bullseye with gcc11 toolchain libs. possible mismatch causes dynamic loader to fail to resolve symbol, leading runtime to mark kernel as incompatible and fall back.

luis: small repro: run bench_server with these flags: `--kv-mode=paged --batch-max-tokens=2048 --kernel-debug=1` then watch kernel selection log. also `strace -eopen` on process while it loads kernels shows `open("/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libatomic.so.1") => ENOENT` on bullseye.

maria: confirmed. adding libatomic to the runtime image fixes the loader error and flash kernel loads. but perf is still regressed even when flash_attn_paged is used. profile shows heavy malloc churn during KV lookups.

ashok: could be ABI/opt flags difference. Did we build wheel with `-flto` or `-fvisibility=hidden`? LTO+libstdc++ sometimes changes inlining and codegen across toolchains and can affect memory layout and allocator behavior.

maria: wheel was built with `CFLAGS=-O3 -march=x86-64 -flto` in the CI Dockerfile to optimize for throughput.

devon: suggestion: produce a debug wheel without LTO and with `-DREDFLASH_PROFILING` and run microbenchmarks: `python -m redwood.attention.bench --seq 1024 --batch 8 --kv-mode paged`. capture `perf top` and heap profile.

maria: ran that. perf top shows hotspots in `kv_index_lookup` and `std::_Hashtable...::_M_rehash_emplace`. heap profile indicates many small allocations (~64-512B) per token. when I force the allocator to jemalloc in the container, allocations drop and latency recovers ~12%.

ashok: hmm allocator interacting with paged KV is plausible. paged mode does many short-lived vector/grow ops; choose jemalloc or bump tcache. we should also look at our batching heuristics - if batch-max-tokens=2048, we might be creating many per-request temporary buffers. can we reuse KV buffers across requests in the worker?

luis: we have a buffer pool but it's keyed by model+seq_len currently. when using paged KV with mixed seq lengths the pool misses a lot. quick patch: pool by (model, bucketed_seq_len) + reuse threshold 1000. local test shows 6% improvement. PR incoming.

devon: great. in parallel we should fix the wheel/toolchain issue: options: 1) rebuild wheels on bullseye-gcc11 image, 2) vendor libatomic into wheel, or 3) ensure runtime images include libatomic. preference?

srebot: incident note created: INC-2026-022 - nightly perf regression on attention kernels. assign to eng-runtime.

maria: plan: 1) short-term: add libatomic to runtime images and deploy, 2) mid-term: rebuild wheels without LTO and with consistent toolchain (or produce manylinux2014 + libatomic vendoring), 3) testing: add a CI job that runs a tiny latency microbenchmark after wheel publish to catch perf regressions earlier.

ashok: also add linker map dump step when building kernels to detect hidden symbol deps: `-Wl,-Map,build/_kernels.map`. saved me before.

devon: thanks. if anyone can validate the libatomic runtime image and luis's pool change on staging, we can roll a canary tomorrow. :thumbsup:

maria: validating now, will post numbers in thread. thanks all.
